semantics: RFC 5545 section 3.8.5.3 semantics. DTSTART is always the first instance and counts toward COUNT (include_dtstart=true), even if it does not match the RRULE; RFC 5545 calls such a recurrence set undefined, and the only example here where DTSTART does not match (case 28, Friday the 13th) removes it with EXDATE. Instances from RRULE and RDATE are unioned (duplicates collapse), then EXDATE values are removed; EXDATE does not change how COUNT is applied. UNTIL is inclusive. A UTC UNTIL is compared with each instance's absolute time, computed in tzid. When tzid is set, dtstart, rdate, exdate, between and expected are wall-clock local times in that zone, so 9:00 AM EDT and 9:00 AM EST are both T090000. When tzid is empty, values are floating, or UTC if they end in Z. Generated dates that do not exist (e.g. February 30) are skipped and not counted. limit=N: compare only the first N instances of the final set (used for unbounded rules; N is how many instances the RFC enumerates). limit=0: compare the complete set. between=null: no window. Each case has exactly one RRULE. Where the RFC gives two alternative RRULEs joined by 'or', they are separate cases with a/b id suffixes and the same expected list.

The ellipses inside each month are expanded; the trailing 'December 1,3,...' ends the enumeration. Unbounded rule: limit is the number of instances the RFC enumerates. Comparison is by limit, not by a between window.

cases.comment: RFC prose: ==> (1998 9:00 AM EST) February 13;March 13;November 13 (1999 9:00 AM EDT) August 13 (2000 9:00 AM EDT) October 13 ... . DTSTART (Tuesday 1997-09-02) does not match the rule. It is still the first instance (include_dtstart=true), and then the RFC's EXDATE removes it, so the RFC's stated output starts at 1998-02-13. cases.name: Every 3 hours from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM on a specific day
cases.comment: RFC prose: ==> (September 2, 1997 EDT) 09:00,12:00,15:00. Verified erratum 3883 applied: the RFC prints UNTIL=19970902T170000Z, which is 13:00 EDT and does not match the description or the stated output. The erratum corrects it to 19970902T210000Z (17:00 EDT). The uncorrected rule is case 33-uncorrected.

cases.name: Every 3 hours from 9:00 AM (RRULE exactly as printed, before erratum 3883)
cases.comment: Derived case, not RFC output. This is the RRULE exactly as printed in RFC 5545, before Verified erratum 3883. UNTIL 19970902T170000Z is 13:00 EDT, so only 09:00 and 12:00 EDT qualify. The RFC's prose result (09:00,12:00,15:00) applies only to the corrected rule, case 33. This case tests that a UTC UNTIL is compared in absolute time.
